key_insight: APEX-SWE is a new benchmark that tests whether frontier AI models can perform economically valuable, real-world software engineering work—especially end-to-end integration across heterogeneous cloud, business apps, and infrastructure.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between narrow task-oriented evaluations and real-world software engineering needs by measuring model ability to execute complex, multi-component engineering tasks that carry economic value.
method: Design APEX-SWE with two novel, real-world task types including Integration tasks (n=100) that require building end-to-end systems across cloud primitives, business applications, and infrastructure.
Run systematic evaluations of frontier AI models on these tasks to assess correctness, completeness, and execution feasibility.
Translate model outcomes into outcome-focused metrics that reflect practical/economic utility for software engineering workflows.
impact: APEX-SWE gives ML practitioners and engineering leaders a realistic yardstick to judge model readiness for production engineering work, guiding model selection, tooling, and investment toward capabilities that deliver measurable economic value.
visual_elements: Pie or stacked bar showing benchmark composition (e.g., % Integration tasks, other task types).
Flow diagram of an Integration task: cloud primitives → business apps → infra → deployed system (end-to-end).
Bar chart comparing multiple frontier models on APEX-SWE performance and an accompanying 'economic value' axis (e.g., estimated time/cost savings).
Icon set highlighting key evaluation axes: correctness, deployability, automation potential, and cost impact.
paper_authors: Abhi Kottamasu, Akul Datta, Aakash Barthwal, Chirag Mahapatra, Ajay Arun
